\defcap{fig29_study_area_map}{Lime-producing provinces of Peru and their cumulative production, January 2016–December 2025: (a) sour lime, (b) sweet lime (MIDAGRI–SISAGRI (accessed \midagridate{})). Circle area is proportional to each province's cumulative production of that cultivar; labels give the five largest provinces and their share of the national total of that cultivar. Symbols show whether a province recorded sour lime only, both cultivars, sweet lime only or no harvest in the period (109 provinces). Dashed rings: ten provinces placed at their department's reference coordinate, including the two sweet-lime-only and the four no-harvest provinces. Boundaries: geoBoundaries gbOpen \cite{runfola2020geoboundaries}, Public Domain, 2008 vintage; neighbouring countries: Natural Earth 1:10m.}
\defcap{fig24_series_with_shocks_sutil}{Monthly national production of sour lime (limón sutil) in Peru, January 2016–December 2025 (MIDAGRI–SISAGRI (accessed \midagridate{})). Grey bands and markers: shock months in the test years 2021–2025, i.e. months whose absolute month-on-month relative change \textbar{}$\Delta$y/y\textbar{} exceeds the 75th percentile of the changes observed up to the forecast origin (December of the previous year); the threshold of each test year is shown above the panel. No month exceeded the threshold in 2021 or 2024.}
\defcap{fig24_series_with_shocks_dulce}{Monthly national production of sweet lime (limón dulce) in Peru, January 2016–December 2025 (MIDAGRI–SISAGRI (accessed \midagridate{})). Grey bands and markers: shock months in the test years 2021–2025, i.e. months whose absolute month-on-month relative change \textbar{}$\Delta$y/y\textbar{} exceeds the 75th percentile of the changes observed up to the forecast origin (December of the previous year); the threshold of each test year is shown above the panel. 14 of the 15 shock months fall in January–March.}
\defcap{fig30_rolling_origin_scheme}{Rolling-origin evaluation design \cite{tashman2000out}. For each test year Y (2018–2025) the forecast origin is December of Y\textminus{}1; trained models use data up to December of Y\textminus{}2 (features from 2016-07; tabular targets from 2016-08; LSTM targets from 2017-01), are tuned and early-stopped on year Y\textminus{}1, and produce twelve one-step-ahead forecasts for year Y. Trained models require at least 36 training months, so windows 2018–2020 (faded) include only the untrained models (Naive, Seasonal Naive, Chronos). The primary ranking pools the windows 2021–2025; a sensitivity analysis specified in the protocol repeats all conclusions on 2023–2025.}
\defcap{fig25_architecture_dual_lstm}{Dual-LSTM with additive (Bahdanau) temporal attention \cite{bahdanau2015neural} used by GC3 and GE. Each branch receives the previous 6 months: branch A the production series and its lags 1, 3 and 6; branch B calendar terms, a time index and lagged climate (NASA POWER) and disaster (INDECI) covariates. GE adds six lagged news features to branch B (dashed box): the monthly mean sentiment score of agricultural news, computed with the pysentimiento RoBERTuito sentiment model \cite{perez2021pysentimiento,perez2022robertuito}, and the monthly number of news items. GC3 and GE are otherwise identical. Trainable parameters: GC3 6,273; GE 6,657.}
\defcap{fig13_mae_normal_vs_shock_bars_sutil}{MAE in normal months (light) and in shock months (hatched; monthly P75 threshold) for each model, sour lime (limón sutil), pooled 2021–2025, with paired bootstrap 95\% CIs \cite{efron1993bootstrap}.}
\defcap{fig13_mae_normal_vs_shock_bars_dulce}{MAE in normal months (light) and in shock months (hatched; monthly P75 threshold) for each model, sweet lime (limón dulce), pooled 2021–2025, with paired bootstrap 95\% CIs.}
